title: docling-project/docling — Get your documents ready for gen AI
content:
Docling simplifies document processing by parsing diverse formats — including advanced PDF understanding — and providing seamless integrations with the generative AI ecosystem.
- 🗂️ Parsing of multiple document formats including PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, Apple Pages, WAV, MP3, WebVTT, Box Notes, email formats (EML, MSG), images (PNG, TIFF, JPEG, ...), LaTeX, DocLang, plain text, and more
- 📑 Advanced PDF understanding incl. page layout, reading order, table structure, code, formulas, image classification, and more
- 🧬 A unified, expressive DoclingDocument representation format
- ↪️ Various export formats and options, including Markdown, HTML, WebVTT, DocLang, DocTags and lossless JSON
- 📜 Support for several application-specific XML schemas including DocLang, USPTO patents, JATS articles, and XBRL financial reports.
- 🔒 Local execution capabilities for sensitive data and air-gapped environments
- 🤖 Plug-and-play integrations incl. LangChain, LlamaIndex, Crew AI & Haystack for agentic AI
- 🔍 Extensive OCR support for scanned PDFs and images
- 👓 Support for several Visual Language Models, such as (GraniteDocling)
- 🎙️ Audio support with Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models
- 🔌 Connect to any agent using the MCP server
- 🌐 Run Docling as a service with the API server (docling-serve)
- 💻 Simple and convenient CLI
- 🎬 Parsing of video files (MP4, AVI, MOV, MKV, and WebM) with an ASR transcript and representative keyframes
- 📄 Parsing of ODF (OpenDocument Format) files for text documents (.odt ), spreadsheets (.ods ), and presentations (.odp )
- 💼 Parsing of XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language) documents for financial reports
- 📧 Parsing of email files (.eml ,.msg )
- 📚 Parsing of EPUB (Electronic Publication) files for e-books
- 🍎 Parsing of Apple Pages (.pages ) documents, both container generations (Pages 5+ and iWork '09)
- 📝 Parsing of plain-text files (.txt ,.text ) and Markdown supersets (.qmd ,.Rmd )
- 📊 Chart understanding (Barchart, Piechart, LinePlot): convert them into tables or code and add detailed descriptions
- 📝 Metadata extraction, including title, authors, references & language
- 📝 Complex chemistry understanding (Molecular structures)
pip install docling
Note: Python 3.9 support was dropped in docling version 2.70.0. Please use Python 3.10 or higher.
Works on macOS, Linux and Windows environments for both x86_64 and arm64 architectures.
More detailed installation instructions are available in the docs.
docling https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.01062
This generates a .md file in the current directory containing structured document content.
You can also use 🥚GraniteDocling and other VLMs via Docling CLI:
docling --pipeline vlm --vlm-model granite_docling https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.01062from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter
source = "https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.09869"  # a document via a local path or URL
converter = DocumentConverter()
result = converter.convert(source)
print(result.document.export_to_markdown())  # output: "## Docling Technical Report[...]"
More advanced usage and configuration options.
Check out Docling's documentation for details on installation, usage, concepts, recipes, extensions, and more.
Go hands-on with our examples, demonstrating how to address different application use cases with Docling.
To further accelerate your AI application development, check out Docling's native integrations with popular frameworks and tools.

report.summary: IBM Research's open-source Docling toolkit parses PDFs, Office files, audio and video into structured Markdown and JSON, streamlining document ingestion for generative AI pipelines.
report.background: Generative AI applications, especially retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), depend on clean, structured text from enterprise documents. Yet much of that data lives in PDFs, slide decks, spreadsheets and scanned images where layout, tables and reading order are lost by naive text extraction. Early open-source parsers handled simple PDFs but struggled with complex layouts, and cloud APIs raised privacy concerns. Docling was started in 2024 by the AI for knowledge team at IBM Research Zurich to solve this 'data preparation' bottleneck. It provides a unified document representation and deep PDF understanding, then exports to Markdown and JSON for LLM consumption. The project is MIT-licensed, hosted by the LF AI & Data Foundation, and has rapidly added formats—audio, video, email, patents—plus integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex and agentic frameworks.
key_points: Docling parses a wide range of inputs: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, images, email, audio (WAV, MP3), video and domain formats like USPTO patents and JATS articles. This breadth means one tool can feed most enterprise document pipelines.

Its advanced PDF engine understands page layout, reading order, tables, code, formulas and images. It also handles charts (converting them to tables or code), chemical structures and metadata extraction, going well beyond simple text scraping.

Output is a unified DoclingDocument representation, exportable as Markdown, HTML, JSON, DocTags or DocLang. Local execution supports sensitive data and air-gapped environments, while OCR and VLM support (e.g., GraniteDocling) improve accuracy on scanned or complex pages.

Plug-and-play integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Crew AI and Haystack, plus an MCP server and docling-serve API, make it easy to drop into RAG pipelines, agents or microservices. A simple CLI and pip install lower the barrier to entry.

Active development: version 2.70.0 dropped Python 3.9; audio/video and ODF/XBRL support are recent additions. The project is backed by IBM Research and the LF AI & Data Foundation, signaling long-term maintenance.
report.impact: Docling addresses a critical bottleneck in generative AI: document ingestion. For the AI industry, it promotes an open, standardized document representation that could reduce reliance on proprietary parsing APIs and improve RAG answer quality, especially for tables and complex layouts. For developers, it saves months of parser engineering and integrates with popular agent frameworks, while local execution helps meet compliance requirements. For regular users, the practical effect is better AI assistants that can accurately read contracts, reports, manuals and even video transcripts. However, performance on messy scans still varies, and the tool remains developer-oriented. Docling's foundation backing and MIT license make it a strong candidate to become the default open-source document loader for LLM applications.
report.tools: To try Docling, start with `pip install docling` and the Python API or CLI. Watch docling-serve for running it as a REST service, the MCP server for agent integration, and GraniteDocling for VLM-powered PDF understanding. Comparable open-source projects include Unstructured, Marker and MinerU for PDF-to-Markdown, and PyMuPDF or Tesseract for lower-level extraction. For RAG, combine Docling with LangChain or LlamaIndex loaders.
